claim: YouVersion's 2026 release was dated October 6, 2026, and reports worldwide daily use of 18.5 million.
quote: Worldwide daily use reached 18.5 million as more people turned to Scripture for comfort, setting the stage for this year's Global Bible Month

claim: YouVersion says daily use grew more than 13% compared with 2025.
quote: Compared to 2025, daily use grew by over 13%, reaching 18.5 million people turning to the Bible each day.

claim: YouVersion says it added more than 160 million installs in 2026, after passing one billion installs in November 2025.
quote: After celebrating one billion installs last November, YouVersion added more than 160 million new installs across its Family of Apps in 2026.

claim: 'Anxiety', 'hope' and 'healing' were among the year's most-searched terms, and 'Psalm 91' was the single most-searched term.
quote: Terms like "anxiety," "hope" and "healing" were among the year's most searched, with "Psalm 91" ranking as the year's single most-searched term.

claim: YouVersion's Family of Apps offers 3,800 Bible versions in 2,400 languages and works with more than 45,000 churches and partners.
quote: YouVersion's Family of Apps offers access to 3,800 different versions of the Bible in 2,400 languages ... The organization works with a global network of more than 45,000 churches and partners

claim: Nearly 3 million people signed up for the 2025 30-Day Bible Challenge. This November the Challenge adds a feature to track progress and see friends' engagement.
quote: In 2025, nearly 3 million people worldwide signed up for the first year of the Challenge. This November, YouVersion hopes its community will build on that momentum, with the Challenge returning with a new feature that lets users track their progress and see how their friends are engaging alongside them.

claim: Bobby Gruenewald, founder and CEO of YouVersion, said the ministry is encouraged by how many people turn to Scripture for answers.
quote: "This year, we've been encouraged by how many people are turning to Scripture for answers to their questions," said Bobby Gruenewald, Founder and CEO of YouVersion.

claim: Global Bible Month in November centers on the 30-Day Bible Challenge, which can be done with a print Bible or an app.
quote: At its heart is the 30-Day Bible Challenge, encouraging people to engage with God's Word every day during November, whether through a favorite print Bible or digitally through an app.

claim: YouVersion is a digital ministry of Life.Church and its Bible apps are free.
quote: YouVersion, a digital ministry of Life.Church, invites everyone into a daily rhythm with God's Word through its free Bible apps.

claim: For comparison, YouVersion's 2025 data named Isaiah 41:10 the most engaged-with verse, with love, anxiety and peace among the top search terms.
quote: Throughout the year, the most searched terms included love, anxiety, and peace, reflecting the questions and concerns weighing most heavily on people's hearts.

claim: YouVersion's 2025 release counted 2.6 million or more people taking the 30-Day Bible Challenge, compared with 'nearly 3 million signed up' in the 2026 release. The metrics differ.
quote: As part of Global Bible Month, more than 2.6 million people took the 30-Day Bible Challenge, with daily Bible use increasing by 19% compared to November 2024.

claim: In 2025, YouVersion's single-day record was more than 19 million people opening the app.
quote: the first Sunday of the month set an all-time record with more than 19 million people opening the app in a single day.

claim: YouVersion's privacy policy lists search history among the data it collects.
quote: Internet or other network activity (browsing history, search history, information on your interaction with our websites, apps, and other services)

claim: YouVersion says it does not sell personal data or share it with advertisers, and that public engagement stats are aggregated.
quote: We do not sell or share your personal data with any third-party advertisers or ad networks for their advertising purposes.

claim: YouVersion says it publishes engagement stats only in aggregated form.
quote: When you see stats we share publicly such as global YouVersion engagement, we make sure to analyze and publish the data in an aggregated form, protecting your privacy

claim: A 2013 essay from the University of Chicago Divinity School criticized YouVersion for combining behavioral data and consumer psychology with Scripture.
quote: As technology is paired with consumer psychology, the way in which we engage religious content is being transformed with the same methods advertisers use to compel us to buy and consume their products.

claim: Ascension released the Catholic Reading Bible: Dyslexia-Friendly Edition. Ascension calls it the first complete Catholic Bible set in the Grace typeface.
quote: Today, Ascension introduced the Catholic Reading Bible: Dyslexia-Friendly Edition, the first complete Catholic Bible to feature the Grace typeface and its associated design principles.

claim: The Grace typeface was developed by 2K/DENMARK, informed by testing with dyslexic readers and work involving the University of Cambridge.
quote: The Grace typeface and its associated design principles were developed specifically for accessible reading by internationally renowned Bible design firm 2K/DENMARK, informed by research, testing with dyslexic readers, and work involving the University of Cambridge.

claim: Grace adds weight near the base of letters and uses lines of no more than 35 characters, ragged-right text and 11-point type.
quote: The Grace typeface uses added weight near the base of letters to help visually anchor them to the line and distinctive details to make similar letterforms easier to differentiate. The Grace design principles incorporate shorter lines of no more than 35 characters, longer paragraphs divided into smaller text blocks, ragged-right alignment to maintain more consistent word spacing, generous 11-point type

claim: The edition uses the RSV-2CE translation, costs $45 and includes ten reading overlays (nine colored, one gray).
quote: The Catholic Reading Bible: Dyslexia-Friendly Edition is available from Ascension for $45.00 and includes a brown leatherlike cover with Smyth-sewn binding, three ribbon markers, nine colored overlays, one gray overlay

claim: Ascension CEO Jonathan Strate cited Dei Verbum on easy access to Scripture.
quote: Dei Verbum teaches that 'Easy access to Sacred Scripture should be provided for all the Christian faithful.' We developed this Bible in that spirit

claim: Grace was first used in Protestant Bibles from Lifeway (CSB) and Crossway (ESV). Its designer made the font nonproprietary.
quote: Typically, his company sells its products to a singular publisher to own, but he intentionally opted to make the Grace font nonproprietary.

claim: Independent studies of earlier dyslexia fonts (OpenDyslexic, Dyslexie) found no gain in reading speed or accuracy. No peer-reviewed results for Grace were found.
quote: So far, the research doesn't really have a lot of evidence showing that these special fonts help kids or adults with dyslexia to read faster or make fewer mistakes.

claim: The Gloo AI Hackathon's Best of Bible Track, powered by YouVersion, went to Envoy Mission, an offline, private Bible app delivered through multilingual AI conversations with seekers.
quote: Best of Bible Track, powered by YouVersion: Envoy Mission, an offline, private Bible ... It is delivered through multilingual AI conversations with seekers around the world.

claim: Track winners received $20,000 each. More than 1,000 builders on more than 115 teams took part, and the grand prize of $100,000 went to Fosterly.
quote: More than 1,000 builders on more than 115 teams took part under this year's theme, "Building Together: Humans, Agents and the Future of Flourishing."

claim: Pray.com launched Pray Production Studio, an AI tool that turns sermons into cinematic video, starting at $19 a month.
quote: PPS is available today with subscription plans starting at $19 per month

claim: A theologian told NPR that Pray.com's AI Bible videos frame Scripture as entertainment.
quote: "I think that the package, the form, situates the Bible as entertainment, as content to be titillated or amused by… Rather than a word that is a divine revelation intended to transform our lives and bring them into accordance with truth, with God and with one another," said Jeffrey Bilbro

claim: Brad East (Abilene Christian University) said turning the Bible into short-form viral content robs it of its power.
quote: The medium matters, East said. For Christians, the Bible is the word of God, and turning that word into short-form viral content robs it of its power.
